behavioral_equivalence.details: Modernized code maintains all core functionality from legacy code including authentication, session management, and discount calculation. Domain logic was properly extracted.

test_coverage.details: BDD scenarios cover most use cases but lack explicit tests for: 1) Database validation failure cases 2) Token generation edge cases 3) Async operation timeouts

compliance_check.details: CFR Part 11 requirements for audit trails are mentioned in scenarios but not implemented in code. Need explicit audit logging implementation.

security_check.details: Hardcoded admin credentials remain (though now in service layer rather than domain). Recommend moving to secure configuration. PII handling appears proper.

performance_analysis.details: Async operations improve scalability. No major performance regressions detected. Token generation remains lightweight.

net10_alignment.details: Properly uses modern .NET features: records, async/await, dependency injection, and configuration system.

items: Audit trail requirement not fully implemented
No rate limiting on authentication attempts

recommendations: Implement proper audit logging for CFR Part 11 compliance
Remove hardcoded credentials or move to secure secrets management
Add rate limiting to prevent brute force attacks
Consider stronger token generation (JWT with proper signing)
Add test cases for async operation failures
Implement input sanitization for SQL injection prevention
rationale: While the modernization is technically sound and functionally equivalent, compliance and security concerns require attention before production deployment.
